title.text: Rivalry Week Look: pick a column

how.text:
Each board is one screen. Each column is one direction, the same in every board: Today (no Look), then A, B and C. Read a column top to bottom to see a direction across the app.

Chat, Settings and You carry no rivalry names, so they wear only the chrome, the same way the Leaderboard does: A's band, B's paper or C's laces.

The home-screen app icon stays the same in every direction. It can't change week to week.

a.text:
A · The banner. No tokens change. A 28px rust band reading RIVALRY WEEK sits under every header and on the launch screen. A rivalry name is a rust caps label above its game: on the Picks kickoff line, on a Live Board row, and in the game sheet, where the trophy follows as a muted line.

Build: weekLook(week) gives each screen "rivalry". One RivalryBand component goes under AppHeader and the Picks header, plus one caps label.

b.text:
B · The paper. The whole app changes paper for the Week. A .look-rivalry class on <html> overrides 8 tokens: background, card, popover, muted, accent, muted-foreground, border/input and settled, with rust darkened to #9c4314 so caps labels still pass 4.5:1 on muted. Pine stays the chosen team. A rivalry name is a rust outline pill with crossed swords, set where the Tiebreaker and Void badges sit. The trophy appears only in the game sheet, under the score.

Build: weekLook sets the class in the root layout, plus one RivalryPill. This direction is the cheapest to build and the most app-wide.

c.text:
C · The program. A 10px pine strip with football laces runs across the top of every screen and frames the launch screen. Rivalry games get top billing: the name in Chivo display type above the matchup on Picks, as the row title on the Live Board, and as the game sheet's headline with "For the <trophy>" under it. Ordinary games stay as they are.

Build: one Laces asset in the header slot, plus a RivalryTitle used in three places. The rows grow by about 20px.
